purpose: Evaluate retaining original 64x64 spatial locations in Lean memory rotary attention after pruning.
candidate: Same automatic YOLO initialization, early-feature points, multi-scale anchor, 25% memory retention, pointer tail, model parameters, frame schedule and CPU FP32 runtime as the corrected CPU-repeat reference. Query rotary frequencies use the full 64x64 grid; every spatial memory key uses its exact source-grid coordinate recovered from the existing spatial plus temporal position embedding. Pointer tokens remain unrotated. Exact lookup fails rather than guessing for unknown or ambiguous positions.
validation: First verify synthetic dense/permuted/pruned positions, temporal offsets, pointer exclusion, fail-closed behavior and context restoration. Replay corrected reference on seq3 with a read-only position observer and require exact masks and token selection receipts. Run candidate seq3 twice without labels, require deterministic masks and position traces, unchanged weights, identical first three masks (before the first previously observed frequency mismatch), preserved token budget and a verified change in later masks. Report any deviations. No full-video scoring until these checks succeed.
constraints: No re-detection or new confidence, adaptive, or mask thresholds; no labels during inference. This is an experimental positional correction, not a trained CMSA module. Existing Lean insurance/history behavior is retained. Its history-fused memory content is a mixture, although it retains the spatial position of its scaffold.
analysis: Compare paired identical-prompt predictions against the CPU-repeat corrected run, report all-present and historical matched-frame Dice and labeled-empty false alarms, and describe GT-prompt native and Lean historical results only as unequal-initialization references. No inference-time use of annotations. Prior sequences were inspected, so outcomes are exploratory.
